name: The Son
role: At God's right hand; volunteers to redeem mankind before the Fall has happened; sole victor of the War in Heaven
description: Category A, with the same Arian/subordinationist controversy as God the Father -- De Doctrina Christiana holds the Son is begotten, not co-eternal, a position modern scholarship (Maurice Kelley's This Great Argument, 1941; Rumrich; Bauman's Milton's Arianism, 1987) links to the poem, though whether the verse text itself fully commits to this is a live debate. In Book VI he alone routs Satan's rebel host, driving them over Heaven's wall. See docs/milton/character-catalog.md §IV and docs/milton/theology-and-sources.md §1.
narrative_function: Wins the War in Heaven single-handedly; volunteers pre-emptively to redeem the Fall God already foresees.
